samples.summary: Row/column reorder is refused whenever ANY merge straddles the freeze, not just ones the move touches — a pre-existing straddle (legacy docs, peers) permanently blocks every reorder
samples.evidence: `moveCells` builds `movedMerges = moveMergeMap(this.merges, ...)` and refuses if *any* entry crosses the freeze pane (sheet.ts:1566-1572). A block that already straddled before the move is remapped unchanged when the move does not touch its rows, so it still straddles and the reorder is refused with `merge-move-frozen` ("Can't move a merged cell across a frozen row or column") even though the user moved unrelated rows. Straddling state is reachable and is NOT repaired on load: `loadFreezePane` (sheet.ts:567-571) and `loadMerges` (588-591) copy the stored values verbatim, and before this change `setFreezePane` stored whatever the user dragged, so any document where a user froze a row through the middle of a merged block is now permanently un-reorderable. The backend has the identical shape: `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` iterates the whole moved map and 409s (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:194-203). The check should be limited to blocks the move actually relocates (as `moveRangeTo` does with `movedMerges` at sheet.ts:2857/2875), or the newly-straddling set (blocks that cross after but not before).

samples.summary: `applyMerge` reads the Yorkie merges record with raw `Object.values`, the exact call the repo's `safeWorksheetRecord*` helpers exist to guard, so a duplicate-key CRDT record throws inside `doc.update`
samples.evidence: `mergeBudgetAdmits(mergeBudgetOf(Object.values(ws.merges)), [span])` runs on the live Yorkie proxy inside `doc.update`. `safeWorksheetRecordValues`/`safeWorksheetRecordEntries` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-record.ts:13-75) exist precisely because `ownKeys` on such a record throws `TypeError: ... duplicate`, and the same file already uses the safe helper for the same field (`getMerges`, yorkie-store.ts:1041). A throw here escapes `doc.update` and aborts every merge write (including the batched paste flush at endBatch, which would take the whole batch down) on any document that hit the duplicate-key condition.

samples.summary: The freeze snap grows the boundary without any bound, so one tall merged block can freeze the entire viewport — and it now fires automatically on inserts/deletes in legacy documents
samples.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges` sets the line to the block's end row/col with no clamp (merging.ts:331-334). A single merge is only capped at `MaxMergedCells = 100000` cells, so `A1:A100000` plus a request to freeze row 1 stores `frozenRows = 100000`, and the renderer then paints a frozen pane larger than the grid can scroll. Worse, this is applied non-interactively: `Sheet.shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1432-1443) and `shiftWorksheetViewState` (worksheet-structure.ts:278-288) snap on every insert/delete, so a legacy document that already has a tall block straddling the freeze has its frozen band silently blown up by an unrelated row insert. A cap (e.g. leave the boundary alone, or refuse, when the snap would exceed some fraction of the sheet) is missing.

samples.summary: Store-level budget refusal silently diverges from `Sheet`'s in-memory merge map: merges the engine believes it wrote are never persisted and vanish on reload
samples.evidence: `applyMerge` returns without writing when the budget refuses (yorkie-store.ts:987-992), but callers in `Sheet` unconditionally update `this.merges` right after `await this.store.setMerge(...)` — `moveRangeTo` (sheet.ts:2969-2970) performs no budget check at all, and `mergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4931-4932) relies on `this.mergeBudget`, a cached value. On a document that is already over budget (created by an older build, or imported), a drag-move drops the source anchors via `deleteMerge` and then has its destination anchors silently rejected: the UI shows the merged blocks until the next load, after which the layout is gone. The store should signal the refusal (return value / throw) so the engine does not record a write that did not happen.

samples.summary: `revalidateCopyBuffer` and `anchorsForRange` copy the full row and column order arrays on every remote change while a clipboard exists
samples.evidence: `anchorsForRange` (sheet.ts:2259-2268) and `revalidateCopyBuffer` (sheet.ts:2275-2280) call `this.store.getRowOrder()` / `getColOrder()`, which in `YorkieStore` materialize whole-axis copies (`return ws.rowOrder ? [...ws.rowOrder] : []`, yorkie-store.ts:667-675 — the backend explicitly notes this is the expensive form). `Worksheet.handleRemoteChange` now calls `revalidateCopyBuffer()` (view/worksheet.ts:5247) on every remote change, so during an active collaboration with anything on the clipboard each peer keystroke copies both order arrays (up to axis coverage). Resolving just the two corner anchors does not need the full arrays.

samples.summary: A refused reorder now skips `this.render()`, so the drag feedback/refusal is not repainted on the refusal path
samples.evidence: `movePromise.then((moved) => { if (!moved) return; ... this.render(); })` — the early return also skips the `this.render()` at line 4681 that previously always ran after a move attempt. `onCleanup` only calls `renderOverlay()`, so any main-canvas state that depended on the post-drag render (and the refusal toast path, which is triggered synchronously by `refuse` inside `moveCells`) is left unrepainted. Harmless if the refusal UI renders itself; worth confirming.

A pre-existing straddle is reachable and unrepaired: loadFreezePane (sheet.ts:567-571) and loadMerges (588-591) copy stored values verbatim and are used on load and remote-change reload (sheet.ts:5403-5404, 5437-5438; view/worksheet.ts:432-433), and legacy migration copies merges + frozenRows/Cols verbatim (worksheet-shape-migration.ts:444-450); concurrent peers (merge below the line on one client, extend freeze on another) can also produce it since the invariant is only enforced per-client (setFreezePane snap at sheet.ts:543-548, PUT merges 409 at worksheet.controller.ts:253-257). The backend mirrors the same over-broad scan (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:192-203, reached from moveAxis at 295-301). verdict.reason: The described code is present verbatim: yorkie-store.ts:989 calls `mergeBudgetAdmits(mergeBudgetOf(Object.values(ws.merges)), [span])` on the live Yorkie proxy, reached from `setMerge` both via `this.doc.update` (line 1006-1008) and via the batched `batchOps` path (line 1000-1002). The duplicate-ownKeys failure mode is real and recognized in this repo: `isDuplicateOwnKeysError` and `safeWorksheetRecordValues/Entries/Keys` exist for exactly this (worksheet-record.ts:13-75) and there is a test simulating the proxy throw (worksheet-lookup.util.spec.ts:95-108). finding.summary: The freeze snap grows the boundary without any bound, so one tall merged block can freeze the entire viewport — and it now fires automatically on inserts/deletes in legacy documents
finding.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges` sets the line to the block's end row/col with no clamp (merging.ts:331-334). A single merge is only capped at `MaxMergedCells = 100000` cells, so `A1:A100000` plus a request to freeze row 1 stores `frozenRows = 100000`, and the renderer then paints a frozen pane larger than the grid can scroll. Worse, this is applied non-interactively: `Sheet.shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1432-1443) and `shiftWorksheetViewState` (worksheet-structure.ts:278-288) snap on every insert/delete, so a legacy document that already has a tall block straddling the freeze has its frozen band silently blown up by an unrelated row insert. A cap (e.g. leave the boundary alone, or refuse, when the snap would exceed some fraction of the sheet) is missing.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. merging.ts:330-335 grows the freeze line to `end(range)` with no clamp; the only ceiling on a span is MaxMergedCells=100000 cells (merging.ts:14, enforced as a cell count at merging.ts:95 and worksheet-settings.ts:163), so a 1-column x 100000-row merge is legal and freezing row 1 stores frozenRows=100000. Nothing downstream clamps it: Sheet.setFreezePane (sheet.ts:543-548) persists the snapped value verbatim, and buildFreezeState (layout.ts:145-152) derives frozenHeight = rowDim.getOffset(frozenRows+1) unbounded, yielding a frozen pane larger than the scrollable body. The non-interactive firing is also real: Sheet.shiftCells snaps and persists after every insert/delete (sheet.ts:1432-1443) and shiftWorksheetViewState does the same on the document model (worksheet-structure.ts:278-288), both unconditionally, so a pre-existing straddling tall block in a legacy/migrated document has the frozen band blown up by an unrelated row insert. I searched the view layer (worksheet.ts:1382-1393, 2968-2978, layout.ts:136-153) and the backend handlers and found no guard, clamp, or refusal that makes this unreachable, so no refutation ground (not-present / already-guarded) applies. The doc comments call the growth intentional, but that does not bound its magnitude, and an unscrollable viewport is user-visible wrong behavior rather than pure style/design, so out-of-scope does not hold either.

finding.summary: Store-level budget refusal silently diverges from `Sheet`'s in-memory merge map: merges the engine believes it wrote are never persisted and vanish on reload
finding.evidence: `applyMerge` returns without writing when the budget refuses (yorkie-store.ts:987-992), but callers in `Sheet` unconditionally update `this.merges` right after `await this.store.setMerge(...)` — `moveRangeTo` (sheet.ts:2969-2970) performs no budget check at all, and `mergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4931-4932) relies on `this.mergeBudget`, a cached value. On a document that is already over budget (created by an older build, or imported), a drag-move drops the source anchors via `deleteMerge` and then has its destination anchors silently rejected: the UI shows the merged blocks until the next load, after which the layout is gone. The store should signal the refusal (return value / throw) so the engine does not record a write that did not happen.

verdict.reason: The claimed code exists exactly as described. yorkie-store.ts:987-992 returns from `applyMerge` without writing when `mergeBudgetAdmits` refuses, and `setMerge` (996-1009) returns `Promise<void>` with no return value or throw in either the batched or unbatched branch, so callers cannot observe the refusal. In sheet.ts, `moveRangeTo` deletes source/overwritten merges (2961-2962) and then does `await this.store.setMerge(...)` immediately followed by `this.merges.set(...)` (2969-2970); I read its full pre-flight section (2827-2902) and it contains only split-source, partial-destination and freeze-pane checks — no merge-budget check at all. `mergeSelection` (4931-4932) likewise records the write unconditionally, gated only by `canMergeSelection`'s test against the cached `this.mergeBudget` (4883), a field derived from the in-memory `this.merges` in `rebuildMergeCoverMap` (862-876), whereas the store recomputes from `root`. No guard elsewhere makes the refusal unreachable: the caps (merging.ts:30,42,86-100) are enforced only by the current writers (store `applyMerge`, xlsx-importer.ts:244-279, canMergeSelection), so a document already over budget (pre-cap/legacy or divergent state) is reachable, and `applyMerge` skips validation entirely when the anchor already exists (`!ws.merges[sref] &&`), never re-validating such a map. On that path a drag-move drops the source merges and silently loses the destination merges, leaving the engine's in-memory merge map and cover map out of sync with the persisted CRDT until reload — a real correctness/data-loss divergence in this lens's lane.

searchedFor: read worksheet.controller.ts PUT /merges handler for any additional aggregate check
finding.summary: `parseMerges` caps per-span cells (100k) and entry count (10k) but nothing caps the product, so a ~250 KB body can still store 1e9 covered cells and make the tab unopenable
finding.evidence: Line 174 rejects a single span over `MaxMergedCells = 100000`; line 141 rejects more than `MaxMergeEntries = 10000` entries. Neither bounds the sum: 10,000 distinct anchors each with `{rs: 100000, cs: 1}` passes both checks (each entry serialises to ~25 bytes, so ~250 KB, far under the 25 MB body limit) yet gives 1e9 total covered cells. `Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap()` — the very function both comments cite as the reason for the caps — inserts one Map entry per covered cell on every document load, so such a stored map is exactly the "document nobody can open again" the guard exists to prevent, and it is only recoverable through another API call. The new entry cap therefore does not close the hole its own doc-comment claims to close; a cumulative `sum(rs*cs)` ceiling is what is missing.

verdict.reason: The cumulative sum(rs*cs) ceiling the finding calls missing exists and is enforced on this exact path. `MaxMergeCoveredCells = 1000000` is defined at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts:42, and `mergeBudgetError` (merging.ts:68-76) rejects any budget whose `coveredCells` exceeds it (lines 72-74) in addition to the entry-count check (lines 69-71). In `parseMerges`, packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:135 declares `let coveredCells = 0`, line 168 accumulates `coveredCells += rs * cs` for every entry, and lines 178-181 call `mergeBudgetError({ entries: entries.length, coveredCells })` after the loop and throw a BadRequestException when it returns a message. The finding's stated bypass — 10,000 anchors each `{rs: 100000, cs: 1}` — totals 1e9 covered cells, exceeds the 1e6 cap, and is rejected at worksheet-settings.ts:179-181. The earlier check at lines 127-133 passing `coveredCells: 0` is only the cheap pre-loop entry-count gate, as its comment (lines 125-126) and the post-loop comment (lines 173-177) state explicitly. The same sum is spent by the other writers through `mergeBudgetAdmits` (merging.ts:86-100), which routes its running `coveredCells` through `mergeBudgetError` at line 99.
